name: speckit-auto-ai
description: Fully automatic AI-powered markdown-to-PDF documentation generation for VS Code
author: Speckit Team

commands.title: Speckit: Discover Models for Custom Provider

speckit.backendUrl.description: Backend API URL for document processing

speckit.autoProcess.description: Automatically process markdown files on save

speckit.includePatterns.description: Glob patterns for files to include in auto-processing

speckit.excludePatterns.description: Glob patterns for files to exclude from processing

speckit.apiKey.description: API key for backend authentication - must match SPECKIT_EXT_API_KEY in infra/docker-compose.yml (dev-key by default). Empty defeats auth entirely (no Authorization header is sent), so every backend call 401s.

speckit.enableDebugLogging.description: Enable verbose debug logging (may log sensitive content)

speckit.debounceMs.description: Debounce delay in milliseconds for file change events

speckit.maxConcurrentProcessing.description: Maximum number of files to process concurrently

speckit.allowRuleBasedFallback.description: Allow falling back to a lower-quality rule-based transform when no AI provider is available or the AI request fails. When off (default), processing fails with a clear error instead, so you notice and fix AI availability rather than silently getting a degraded PDF/board.

speckit.enableCopilotProgressTracking.description: Auto-provision .github/copilot-instructions.md (and a .gitignore entry) with live task-progress-tracking instructions in Speckit projects, and watch for the resulting signal files, so the Kanban board can show a task as "In Progress" while Copilot works on it, not just "Done" once its checkbox is saved.

speckit.preferredModelId.description: Substring (case-insensitive) matched against the id/family/name of the Copilot models available to this extension, e.g. "gpt-4o" or "o1" - if it matches, that model is tried first instead of whichever one Copilot returns by default. Leave empty to use the default. See "Speckit: Show Extension Logs" for the exact ids/families available in your session.

items.patternErrorMessage: Must be copilot, claude, kiro, generic, custom, or custom:<id of an entry in speckit.customModels>

speckit.providerPriority.markdownDescription:
Legacy/manual override for the order in which AI providers are tried. Hidden from the Settings UI because the try order is owned by the "Speckit: Manage AI Providers" panel, which stores it outside settings; a value here is only used until that panel saves an order.

Tokens: `copilot`, `claude`, `kiro`, `generic`, one `custom:<id>` per entry in `#speckit.customModels#`, or a bare `custom` for every model not placed individually. Rule-based fallback isn't in this list - see `#speckit.allowRuleBasedFallback#`.

id.description: Stable identifier for this entry - any unique string (e.g. "local-ollama"). Used internally to target this entry when saving discovered models; not shown anywhere.

enabled.description: Whether this entry is tried at all. Only takes effect if "custom" is also present in speckit.providerPriority.

name.description: Display name shown in logs/notifications (e.g. "Local Ollama", "Ollama Cloud"). Falls back to the model name if left empty.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of an OpenAI-chat-completions-compatible endpoint, up to but not including "/chat/completions" - e.g. "http://localhost:11434/v1" for a local Ollama server (Ollama exposes this automatically), or "https://ollama.com/v1" for Ollama Cloud.

modelName.description: The model actually sent in each request's "model" field, exactly as the endpoint expects it (e.g. "llama3.1:70b", not the product name "ollama"). Run "Speckit: Discover Models for Custom Provider" to list what this endpoint actually supports instead of typing one by hand.

apiKey.description: Sent as "Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>" when non-empty. Leave empty for a local server (e.g. Ollama) that doesn't require one.

models.description: Populated automatically by "Speckit: Discover Models for Custom Provider" - the model ids this endpoint reported as available, for reference. Not read for anything other than display; edit modelName above to actually change what's used.

speckit.customModels.markdownDescription:
### ➜ [Manage AI providers](command:speckit.manageCustomModels)

The one place to add custom models (base URL, API key, endpoint testing, model discovery) **and** drag every provider - Copilot, Claude, Kiro, Generic and each custom model - into the order they should be tried.

VS Code cannot render an array-of-objects setting, so this row only offers raw JSON; the panel writes it for you.

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
